nodes.description: A patent document titled "Real-time ad-hoc spam filtering of email" describing a multi-pass ad-hoc spam message filtering approach.

A filtering approach that dynamically generates a temporary classifier during a first pass based on results of a previously applied message filter that sorts messages into folders, then uses the classifier in a second pass to retrospectively inspect messages for misclassification.
A model generated during the first pass analysis of messages, configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory location and purged after use.

A message filter configured to sort messages into different message folders and to store first classification data in a persistent store; it may execute on a network device distinct from a client device.<SEP>A message filter that previously sorts messages into a plurality of different message folders and stores first classification data in a persistent store.<SEP>A message filter that sorts messages into different message folders and stores first classification data in a persistent store; it is automatically executed independent of user action.
A filter configured to generate a classification model based on a first pass analysis and use it to perform a second pass on sorted messages to identify misclassified messages.

A device distinct from a client device on which the first message filter is configured to execute.<SEP>A device comprising a transceiver to send and receive data over a network and a processor operative to perform message management actions including multi-pass filtering.<SEP>A device configured to receive messages, assign them to message folders using the first message filter, and communicate the messages over a network.
A component of the network device operative to perform actions such as first pass analysis, second pass analysis, displaying misclassification identification, and purging the classification model.
A component of the network device that sends and receives data over a network.

A plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted by the first message filter and inspected by the multi-pass filter.<SEP>Different folders into which messages are sorted; a message may be identified as sorted into an incorrect message folder.
A generated identification of sorted messages that might be misclassified, displayed so a user can move misclassified messages to a different folder.
A memory-resident-only location where the generated classification model resides, not stored on disk or another persistent data store.

A storage component in which the first message filter stores first classification data.<SEP>A persistent data store where the first message filter stores first classification data.<SEP>A storage location where the first message filter stores first classification data.

A device on which the first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter may occur entirely, and on which the first pass is executed.<SEP>A user's device on which the classification model is maintained in memory and where the first and second passes may occur entirely.<SEP>A device on which the multi-pass message filter is executed, containing a non-persistent memory store for second classification data and an interface enabling user selection of the filter.

A storage medium storing instructions, referenced in claims describing the multi-pass message filter and classification model.<SEP>A medium including data and instructions whose execution on a computing device provides for managing messages.

A message received in plurality and sorted into message folders, and whose delivery is managed by the method.<SEP>An email or similar item sorted into folders, analyzed for sender information, headers, subject, originating network address, contents, and attachments.
Information within messages read during the first pass, including the sender's address and whether it is in an address book associated with a recipient.
Headers within messages read during the first pass, including a subject and an originating network address.
The content of messages read during the first pass analysis.
Attachments within messages read during the first pass analysis.

An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders, used in analysis of whether a message sender's address is present.<SEP>An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders; a message sender's address in it may be analyzed to generate second classification data.

A person whose mail folders are scanned and who is presented a list of messages that might be misclassified so they can move messages to different folders.<SEP>A person enabled to move an identified message to another message folder and to select execution of the multi-pass message filter through an interface.
A recipient associated with the message folders and with an address book used in classification analysis.

A message filtering method that executes a first pass and a second pass, can be trained by generating second classification data, and may employ a Naive Bayes classifier.<SEP>A message filter executed in multiple passes on a client device; a first pass trains the filter by generating second classification data, and a second pass uses that data to score each message.
A classifier that the multi-pass message filter may employ.
Classification data stored in a persistent store by the first message filter.<SEP>Data stored in a persistent store by the first message filter.

Classification data generated by the first pass of the multi-pass message filter to train the multi-pass message filter; it can be deleted so that it is no longer accessible.<SEP>Data generated by the first pass of the multi-pass message filter to train the filter; it resides exclusively in a non-persistent memory store and is used to score messages in the second pass.
A generated classification model produced based on an analysis of at least which message folder a message currently resides.
One of a plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted, and whose current residence of a message is analyzed for generating the second classification model.
A memory store on the client device where second classification data resides exclusively and from which it is deleted upon providing the display of information.
A plurality of messages received and sorted into message folders, each scored by the multi-pass message filter.
A communications network over which messages are communicated to message folders.
An interface on the client device through which a user can select execution of the multi-pass message filter.
A header of a message that may be analyzed to generate second classification data.
The content of a message that may be analyzed to generate second classification data.

edges.description: The patent document US8069128B2 describes a multi-pass ad-hoc spam message filtering approach.
The multi-pass filtering approach dynamically generates a temporary classification model during a first pass.
The multi-pass filtering approach generates its classifier based on results of a previously applied first message filter that sorts messages into folders.
The second multi-pass message filter generates a classification model based on first pass analysis and uses it in a second pass.
The generated classification model is configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory location.
The classification model is maintained within memory on a user's client device.
The processor purges the generated classification model from the non-persistent memory location.
The first message filter sorts messages into a plurality of different message folders.
The first message filter stores first classification data in a persistent store.
The first message filter is configured to execute on a network device distinct from a client device.<SEP>The network device assigns messages to folders using the first message filter.
The first message filter is configured to store first classification data in a persistent store.
The first message filter sorts the plurality of messages into a plurality of different message folders.
The first message filter sorts the plurality of received messages into different message folders.
The first message filter sorts the plurality of messages into different message folders.
The second multi-pass message filter performs a second pass on the sorted message folders to retrospectively inspect messages.
The processor performs first pass analysis and second pass analysis using the second multi-pass message filter.
The processor readable storage medium includes instructions that enable executing the multi-pass message filter.
Executing the first pass and second pass of the multi-pass message filter occurs entirely on a client device.
The network device comprises a transceiver to send and receive data over a network.
The network device comprises a processor operative to perform message management actions.
The network device communicates the messages over the network to the message folders.
The network device communicates messages over the network to the plurality of different message folders.
The network device receives the plurality of messages and assigns them to message folders using the first message filter.
The processor generates and displays the misclassification identification of sorted messages.
The misclassification identification is displayed such that at least one misclassified message can be moved to a different message folder.
The user can move misclassified messages to a different message folder.
The recipient is associated with the message folders.
The plurality of messages are sorted and assigned into the different message folders.

The first classification data is stored in a persistent store.

Messages contain sender information read during the first pass analysis.

Messages contain contents read during the first pass analysis.
Messages contain attachments read during the first pass analysis.

The multi-pass message filter scores each message and identifies messages sorted into an incorrect message folder.
